ai.description: The Niluvase Dancing Frog is a small species (20–25 mm) with a brown, granular dorsum and pale yellow flanks. It is distinguished by elongated, white-tipped digits and characteristic foot-flagging.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus niluvasei* is best distinguished by the unique, bright white, spade-shaped glandular patch on the inner side of its thighs, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus niluvasei* inhabits the riparian zones of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found along rocky, shaded streams at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.behavior: The Niluvase dancing frog is primarily diurnal, with males performing rhythmic "foot-flagging" displays to attract mates and defend their territories along forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus niluvasei* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of eggs in hidden, subterranean nests within stream beds.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus niluvasei* is endemic to the central Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, typically found near forest streams at elevations between 200 and 800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Niluvase Dancing Frog produces a high-pitched, short, and repetitive "ticking" call, typically heard near fast-flowing, rocky streams in the Western Ghats.
